definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese game of tossing and catching small fabric bags filled with beans or pellets, similar to juggling. Also refers to the beanbags themselves.

examples.english: I learned otedama (beanbag juggling) from my grandmother.

examples.japanese: お{手玉|てだま}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧5⟦つ→つ：01004_tsu⟧⟦{使|つか}って→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦{遊|あそ}ぶ→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{難|むずか}しい→難しい：00517_muzukashii⟧。

notes:
TRADITIONAL GAME:
・Traditionally played by girls
・Often accompanied by ⟦{童謡|どうよう}→童謡：03480_douyou⟧ (children's songs)
・Passed down through generations

THE BAGS:
・Filled with ⟦{小豆|あずき}→小豆：10209_azuki⟧ (azuki beans), ⟦{数珠玉|じゅずだま}→数珠玉：noentry⟧ (Job's tears seeds), or plastic pellets
・Made from colorful fabric, often in ⟦{俵|たわら}→俵：noentry⟧⟦{型|かた}→型：02146_kata⟧ (bale shape)
・Typically play with 3-5 bags

PLAYING STYLES:
・⟦{振|ふ}り{玉|だま}→振り玉：noentry⟧ (toss and catch from same hand)
・⟦{寄|よ}せ{玉|だま}→寄せ玉：noentry⟧ (gather scattered beanbags)
・Various patterns with counting songs

CULTURAL NOTE:
・One of the ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{遊|あそ}び→遊び：01285_asobi⟧ (traditional Japanese games)
・Often taught at お⟦{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧ (New Year) events
・Part of cultural preservation activities in schools
